step1_analysis.description: A cross-coupled CMOS inverter pair (XM1-XM4) that provides negative resistance to sustain oscillation in an LC tank. XM5 acts as a MOS varactor for frequency tuning, with its capacitance controlled by the voltage at LABEL_NET_0.

paper_reference.title: Frequency Dependence on Bias Current in 5-GHz CMOS VCOs: Impact on Tuning Range and Flicker Noise Upconversion

sky130_expected.calculation: With an added 1nH inductor and 1pF capacitor, f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). Parasitic capacitance of the 5um/0.5um transistors adds ~50fF.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The ideal LC tank resonates at 5.03 GHz. Transistor parasitics slightly lower this frequency, aligning perfectly with the paper's 5 GHz target.

sky130_expected.calculation: The cross-coupled inverters will swing nearly rail-to-rail, limited by the tank's parallel resistance and transistor saturation voltages.
sky130_expected.reasoning: At VDD=1.8V, a healthy LC oscillator typically achieves a differential swing close to 2*VDD, but single-ended swing is bounded by 0 and 1.8V.

p_dc.description: DC power consumption of the oscillator core

sky130_expected.calculation: The inverters are DC-shorted by the inductor, biasing them near VDD/2 (~0.8V). I_dc ≈ 2 * 0.5 * u_n * C_ox * (W/L) * (V_bias - V_th)^2 ≈ 200uA. P_dc = 1.8V * 200uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Without a tail current source, the bias current is determined by the short-circuit current of the inverters at their switching threshold.

phase_noise.description: Phase noise at a specific offset frequency (e.g., 1 MHz)

sky130_expected.calculation: Dependent on tank Q-factor and active device noise. Assuming Q=10.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard phase noise for integrated LC VCOs in this frequency range.

tuning_range.description: Frequency variation across the full varactor tuning voltage range

sky130_expected.calculation: Delta_C from XM5 varactor is ~15fF. Delta_f ≈ f_osc * (Delta_C / (2 * C_total)).
sky130_expected.reasoning: With a large fixed 1pF tank capacitor, the tuning range provided by a single 5um/0.5um varactor is relatively small.

step3_testbench.description: Transient and OP analysis to measure the oscillation frequency, amplitude, and DC power consumption of the VCO core. An ideal LC tank is added to enable oscillation, and a short current pulse is used to kickstart it.
step3_testbench.spice:
* VCO Core Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 N0 N1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N0 N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N1 N0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N1 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 LABEL_NET_0 N1 N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}

* Supplies and Biasing
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9
* Tie N2 to LABEL_NET_0 to configure XM5 as a MOS varactor
VN2 N2 LABEL_NET_0 0

* LC Tank (Resonates at ~5 GHz)
L1 N0 N1 1nH
C1 N0 N1 1pF
R1 N0 N1 10k

* Differential Output Voltage
B1 Ndiff 0 V=V(N0)-V(N1)

* Kickstart Pulse to initiate oscillation
I_kick N0 N1 PULSE(0 1m 0.1n 10p 10p 10p 20p)

.control
  * DC Operating Point for Power
  op
  let p_dc = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
  print p_dc

  * Transient Analysis for Oscillation Metrics
  tran 1p 10n
  
  * Measure Oscillation Frequency (Time for 1 cycle between 20th and 21st zero-crossing)
  meas tran t1 trig v(Ndiff) val=0 rise=20 targ v(Ndiff) val=0 rise=21
  let f_osc = 1 / t1
  print f_osc

  * Measure Peak-to-Peak Amplitude
  meas tran vmax max v(Ndiff) from=5n to=10n
  meas tran vmin min v(Ndiff) from=5n to=10n
  let v_pp = vmax - vmin
  print v_pp
  
  quit
.endc
